claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure.
The as-synthesized HfNbTiVAl10 heterostructure includes nanoscale precipitates.
The as-synthesized HfNbTiVAl10 heterostructure includes grain-boundary distributions and phase inhomogeneities.
High-resolution imaging and diffraction data can be used to extract microstructural descriptors for the model.
A physics-informed machine-learning model integrating hierarchical descriptors can predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior of HfNbTiVAl10.
Variations in grain size mediate dislocation dynamics and crack propagation.
Precipitate morphology mediates dislocation dynamics and crack propagation.
The distribution of phase boundaries mediates dislocation dynamics and crack propagation.
Directly linking multiscale structural features to dislocation motion, crack nucleation, and crack propagation can avoid full-scale finite-element simulations.
Avoiding full-scale finite-element simulations will produce faster convergence of mechanical-property predictions.
The proposed model will reduce computational time by roughly an order of magnitude relative to established simulations.
The proposed model will improve predictive accuracy by approximately 10–20% relative to established simulations.
Conventional finite-element and phenomenological constitutive models require extensive simulation time and iterative calibration.
Inadequate capture of hierarchical descriptors may prevent the proposed model from outperforming the baseline.
Unmodeled phase transformations or severe anisotropy may prevent the proposed model from outperforming the baseline.
Failure to obtain at least a 10% accuracy improvement and a tenfold computational-time reduction in blind independent testing would falsify the hypothesis.
